answer: For standard plans, you must submit a reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. For group corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. (Note: An archived 2024 rule previously specified 15 days from the date of discharge [3].)
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

For retail plans, pre-existing diseases carry a 36-month waiting period unless explicitly waived in writing [3][5]. Under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is reduced to 24 months [5]. Waiting periods run continuously from the date of first policy commencement provided coverage does not lapse for more than 30 days [1].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

The no-claim bonus for the Aurora Gold plan is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. The accumulated bonus is not reduced by a claim, but it stops accumulating for that year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment as IVF, assisted reproduction, and infertility treatments are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the issue to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is still unsatisfactory or they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan covers air ambulance up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India on prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, and there is no separate waiting period for it [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. It lasts for 15 days from the receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. During this timeframe, a policyholder who cancels receives a premium refund minus the proportionate risk premium for the cover period, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You get 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a medical procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid [1][5]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% (₹10,000 per day) [1][2]. Because the room cost of ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, proportionate deduction applies based on an eligibility ratio of 0.667, meaning only a reduced proportion of applicable billed charges will be payable [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added to the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but cannot be added to the Bronze plan [1]. When adding a parent, the policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].

Your waiting period credit will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase or excess in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on that incremental amount [1][2].

To continue coverage for your baby beyond the first 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to your policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth to receive guaranteed-issue enrollment without medical underwriting [1]. Additionally, if you need to submit a reimbursement claim for the delivery, you must file it within 30 days of discharge and submit post-hospitalisation bills within 15 days of the end of your plan's post-hospitalisation period [3].

The out-patient benefit (OPD rider) is not available on the Bronze plan [1]. However, the provided sources do not specifically mention out-patient physiotherapy, so whether it can be reimbursed cannot be fully answered from the provided sources [1][3].
Under the Silver plan, having a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points, but does not reset it to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the maternity benefit limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, your out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

No, knee replacement is not covered immediately for general conditions, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1][5]. However, if the knee replacement is required following an accident, it is covered immediately from day one [1][2][5].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount—which offers up to an additional 15% at renewal—is applied last, after the 30% cap, and is the only discount that may exceed it [1][3][5].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied [2][3]. Your option is to apply for reimbursement with pre-approval [3][5], but the claim is payable on reimbursement only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1]. Denial of cashless access is not a rejection of the claim [4].

The deadline to respond depends on the type of claim:

* For general reimbursement claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond, after which Aurora closes the claim [2][5].
* For motor insurance claims, you have 30 days from the date of the query to respond [4].

Under current guidelines, a planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3]. However, the sources disagree, as an archived 2024 document states the deadline is 48 hours before admission [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If Aurora raises a query on the claim, the clock restarts once the queried document is supplied [1]. (An archived 2024 document previously listed this timeline as 30 days from the last document [3].)
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at any age [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Silver plan has no co-payment for insured members below the age of 60 [2].

Across the four plans, pre-hospitalisation cover is 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. Post-hospitalisation cover across the four plans is 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days, respectively [1].

You should choose the Gold plan, as it removes room-rent sub-limits and covers dependent parents-in-law [1][3]. The Platinum plan also covers dependent parents-in-law [1], though room-rent details specific to Platinum are not provided in the sources.

Under the policy, dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is noted as not covered by any plan [1].

You will lose your accumulated benefits—including waiting periods and no-claim bonuses—if you do not pay before the grace period expires [2][3]. The grace period is 30 days from the renewal due date for annual policies and 15 days for policies paid in instalments [1]. Once the grace period expires, the policy is treated as fresh, meaning all waiting periods restart and accumulated no-claim bonuses are lost [2].

Accumulated points can convert to a renewal-premium discount at a rate of 1,000 points for a 5% discount (capped at 15%) [3].
